items.title: ON Semiconductor Stock Is Already Half Off Its High, So How Low Could A Market Shock Take It?
items.summary: ON Semiconductor (ON) stock trades near $67, about 50% below its 52-week high. It lost 43.7% over the trailing three months, ending with a 9.0% fall on September 16. Yet it is still up 38.4% over the trailing twelve months, against 15.5% for the S&P 500. The company's latest results show a business still shrinking but recovering, not one in trouble.

items.title: MCHP's Analog AI Deal Gains Momentum: Can It Outpace NXPI & TXN?
items.summary: Microchip Technology expands its edge-AI push as AnalogAI adopts SST's memBrain SAGE IP for ultra-low-power processors in robots, drones and vehicles.

items.title: Is This Applied Materials Dip The Same Bet It Used To Be?
items.summary: Applied Materials (AMAT) has fallen about 21% from its August high, and the question is whether to buy it. Its own history says dips this size have usually been worth buying, and its valuation argues the other way. The history is specific, so start there.

items.title: Applied Materials Stock Already Fell Without A Shock, So What Would A Real One Do?
items.summary: Applied Materials (AMAT) stock fell 7.1% in its latest session, to about $424. It sits 41% below the high it set within the past year, after a twelve-month run in which it returned 151% against 17% for the S&P 500. It did not fall on a bad quarter, and that is what makes the next leg hard to size.

items.title: Should You Buy Cirrus Logic Stock Because Its Buyback Got Cheaper?
items.summary: Cirrus Logic (CRUS) stock has fallen about 27% in three months and trades roughly a third below its 52-week high. Investors are weighing a PC year that just got pushed out against a share count that keeps shrinking anyway. The buyback behind that is sturdier than the tape suggests: third in line for the cash, and still comfortably funded.

items.title: Texas Instruments Is Up 55% in 2026: This Is the Secret Tech Stock You’re Missing Out On
items.summary: While Wall Street obsesses over AI compute chips, one analog giant has quietly outpaced the S&P 500 by a factor of five this year, and the reason has nothing to do with artificial intelligence.

items.title: Is Applied Materials Stock Amplifying A Risk You Already Own?
items.summary: Applied Materials (AMAT) has added 6.1% over the last five trading days, while the S&P 500 gained 0.1%, and a run like that pulls money in. The five-day move is not the question here. What matters is what this stock does to your money every time the market moves, because it travels much further than the index in both directions.

items.title: Can Monolithic Power's GFS Production Deal Drive Future Growth?
items.summary: MPWR expands manufacturing with GlobalFoundries, adding capacity for power solutions across AI, automotive and data centers.
